difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 447-450 (book Lemma 8.1.2): transporting an integer in the circle code along the generating loop yields its successor, and along the inverse loop its predecessor. The statement is arithmetic about a transport, and the proof (source lines 451-460) has to carry it out through three rewrites: the composition rule for transport, the computation of the action of the code family on the loop as the successor equivalence, and the computation of transport along the univalent image of that equivalence; only then does the arithmetic appear. The second equation is then obtained by the general fact that transports along a path and its inverse are mutually inverse, which is exactly why the second half costs no computation. Which rewrite supplies which factor is the whole content and the statement shows none of it.
